Oregon law sets out when a person occupying land can claim title by adverse possession, and how an owner can remove someone who has no right to be there.

What the official sources say

  • ORS 105.620(1)(a): adverse possession of fee simple title requires actual, open, notorious, exclusive, hostile and continuous possession for 10 years (including predecessors in interest). (ORS 105.620; source)
  • ORS 105.620(1)(b): the possessor must have had, at first entry, an honest belief of being the actual owner, with an objective basis and reasonable under the circumstances, continuing throughout the vesting period. (ORS 105.620; source)
  • ORS 105.620(1)(c): each element must be proved by clear and convincing evidence. (ORS 105.620; source)
  • ORS 105.620(2)(a): possession is 'hostile' if under claim of right or with color of title; color of title means a claim under a written conveyance or by operation of law from one claiming under a written conveyance. The page text shown does not make payment of property tax an element. (ORS 105.620; source)

Oregon statutes set the basic rules between landlords and tenants, including deposits, notices and what happens when a rental is sold.

What the official sources say

  • ORS 90.320(1) habitability list (opened page): landlord must maintain effective waterproofing/weather protection, plumbing, approved water supply with hot and cold running water, adequate heating, electrical lighting, safe and clean grounds, garbage receptacles, floors/walls/ceilings/stairs in good repair, and fire-safety including a working smoke alarm at start of tenancy. (ORS 90.320; source)
  • ORS 90.300(7)(b): the holder of the landlord's interest at the time the tenancy terminates is responsible to the tenant for any security deposit or prepaid rent (relevant on sale). (ORS 90.300; source)
  • ORS 90.322(1): landlord may enter to inspect, make repairs, supply services, or exhibit the unit to prospective purchasers, mortgagees, tenants, workers or contractors; emergency entry needs no notice or consent. Landlord and tenant may agree to entry without notice at reasonable times to show the unit to a prospective buyer if the agreement meets statutory conditions. (ORS 90.322; source)
  • ORS 90.300: a tenant's claim to the security deposit or prepaid rent is prior to the claim of a creditor of the landlord; ORS 90.300(14) requires the accounting or refund to be delivered by personal delivery, first class mail or, if allowed, email. (ORS 90.300; source)
